locator: I q.10 a.2 co.: ratio aeternitatis consequitur immutabilitatem, sicut ratio temporis consequitur motum
interpretation: The notion of eternity follows immutability as the notion of time follows motion; with a.1 (what is altogether immutable has neither succession nor beginning nor end, the two marks of eternity). Read as: what is moved in no respect is eternal. Eternal is a primitive predicate whose content a.1 gives; only this sufficient condition is formalized.
